title: Data sources: reading infrastructure you did not create

videos.script: Ana does not own the network she deploys into. The network team built it by hand, with the AWS CLI, before she wrote any Terraform. She still has to put her servers inside it. {{network}} Copying the VPC id into her files works until the network is rebuilt. Writing the VPC as a resource builds a second network. What she needs is a way to ask. {{ask}} That is a data block. It sends a query through the provider and keeps the answer. It never creates anything, and a destroy never touches what it read. {{data}} The question is when the answer arrives. Usually during the plan, so the real values are there for you to review. Sometimes it has to wait for something the same apply creates, and then the plan says so. {{timing}} And a query is a promise somebody else keeps. A new image appears, and your server is suddenly marked for replacement. A colleague copies a tag, and your plan stops with two matches. {{breaks}} By the end of this lesson you will read what other people built, know when Terraform reads it, and write lookups that fail loudly instead of quietly. {{end}}
